title: When the Detention Turns
premise: Sebastian Vane, a scholarship student at Ashgrove Academy, is paired with his nemesis—golden-boy Julian Marsh, heir to the school board's founding family—for a semester project on the academy's history. Digging through archives, they uncover records of vanished scholarship students and a trust fund quietly drained by the board. As their rivalry thaws into something neither will name, Sebastian must choose between the safe invisibility he's clung to and exposing a truth that could expel them both. In the end, they broadcast the evidence at graduation, Julian renounces his inheritance, and Sebastian finally stops counting days and starts counting people.
about_author: Ada Whitlock taught high school English for a decade before trading red pens for manuscripts, and her stories still smell faintly of chalk dust and detention slips. She writes about sharp-tongued kids who find families in the unlikeliest places.

chapters.title: The Sentence
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Opening with detention—the only place Ashgrove's scholarship kids and legacy kids breathe the same air—Sebastian catalogs his 214 days until freedom. When Ms. Okafor pairs him with Julian Marsh for the Founders' Archive project, both boys protest and lose. The beat: resentment sharpened by reluctant proximity.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Kept
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Working late in the archive, they find enrollment ledgers with names inked out mid-semester—and a trust disbursement trail that doesn't add up. Their bickering turns into real collaboration; Julian admits he's never wanted the empire he's inheriting. The beat: wary alliance forming over shared discovery.

chapters.title: The Price of the Name
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. The board catches wind: Julian's father offers him everything he's ever resented if he hands over the ledgers, while Sebastian faces a scholarship revocation threat. A near-kiss in the archive collapses under the weight of what exposure would cost each of them. The beat: love against duty, duty winning for now.

chapters.title: Graduation Day
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Out of time and options, they splice the evidence into the commencement slideshow. The auditorium erupts as vanished students' names are read aloud; the board fractures, Julian publicly refuses his inheritance, and Ms. Okafor reveals she fed them the first ledger deliberately. Sebastian walks out not alone, counting people instead of days. The beat: found family claimed out loud.
